findings.title: The new passed-state check runs outside the per-tab error guard of the page, so a throw in forecastOf would escape apply() and the minute timer instead of being contained

subject.name: forecastIsPast in renderAll and the minute timer

evidence.value: forecastPassed = forecastIsPast();  (after the RENDERERS.forEach try/catch, not inside it)
setInterval(() => { renderHeader(); fillPickers(); if (forecastIsPast() !== forecastPassed) renderAll(); }, 60000);

An hourly entry whose main is the JSON object {valueOf: 1, toString: 1} makes Number(h.main) at site/index.html:878 throw TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value. The plausible malformed shapes (null, a string, a number, {}, [null], a non-string hour, main as a numeric string or [1], an unparseable hour) all degrade without throwing.

findings.impact: The design of the page is that each tab draws in its own try/catch, so bad data costs one tab. CLAUDE.md adds that the page suite fails on any unexpected console.error. forecastOf is safe inside forecastTile and renderUsage. The copy at line 1004 is not guarded, though. Any throw there leaves apply() and the onSnapshot callback uncaught after the panels are drawn, leaves forecastPassed stale, and repeats as an uncaught error every minute from the timer. The only trigger found is a contrived leaf in an admin-written store that the exporter fills with round() integers, so the practical risk is low.
findings.remediation: Wrap the passed-state computation in the same kind of guard: for example, make forecastIsPast return false on any exception, or compute it inside a try in renderAll. Optionally compute Date.now() once per render and pass it to both the tiles and forecastIsPast. That also closes the millisecond window in which a tile drawn just before the forecast passes is never redrawn with the passed marker. Optionally coerce hourly main and sub only when typeof is number.

follow_ups.ref: justified-improvement: reset-unknown state vs AC-80 wording
follow_ups.note: When the reset of the latest hit is unrecorded, the page shows a duration (2 h 30 min after reset), not a clock time. This is a justified-improvement (round-1 CR-PBI013-02 asked for it), because the alternative time would be earlier than the limit could reset. AC-80 says a time labelled as an estimate, so the owner may want to record this case when settling A-34.

A hit with no reset before it is still timed from the first hour in the recorded hourly series. When usage spans more than 168 hours, the exporter starts that series at the truncation point (exporters/export_sessions.py:377, 548), so the gap is a lower bound. FORECAST_HOW says first hour with recorded usage, which is honest. It is not a finding; worth noting in the method record of the owner.

The non-list usage.hourly throw in usageChart (inside the per-tab guard) and the one-off scroll reset when the timer redraws are both fair notes. Neither blocks. The redraw costs no more than a store change, which the 10-minute refresh loop already causes.
